program: MMus Creative Practice (focuses: Sonic Arts; Popular Music Composition and Production; Audiovisual Cultures; Practice Research)
accreditationStatus: Degree awarded by Goldsmiths, University of London (recognised UK degree-awarding body). Replaces the former separately-titled MMus Sonic Arts pathway.
durationEcts: 1 year full-time / 2 years part-time; 180 UK credits (= 90 ECTS)
whatYouStudy: 'Specialist focuses in popular music composition and production, sonic arts and audiovisual' cultures. Students select two focuses. Compulsory: MMus Project (60 credits) and Expanding Your Practice (60 credits). Optional modules (60 credits) include 'Advanced Strategies in Creative Music Production', Filmmaking and Music Research, Improvisation, Music Management.
entryRequirements: 'An undergraduate degree of at least 2:2 standard in Music or related subject.' 'Your qualification should comprise a substantial relevant practical/creative element.' Goldsmiths also states: 'Students might also be considered for some programmes if they aren't a graduate or their degree is in an unrelated field, but have relevant experience and can show ability to work at postgraduate level.'
acceptsNonMusic: PARTIALLY — 'Candidates without music degrees may be considered if showing ability to work at postgraduate level.' The quoted wording is discretionary and hinges on the portfolio; the required 'substantial relevant practical/creative element' is the real gate.
portfolioSpec: 'Four to six separate pieces' of 'recent original creative work, (audio, video or other formats as appropriate)', supplied as 'links to streamable content'. No maximum duration specified.
auditionSpec: No audition mentioned on the programme page. Goldsmiths states generally: 'Admission to many programmes is by interview, unless you live outside the UK' — an overseas applicant would normally not be interviewed.
otherFees: Goldsmiths requires international students to make an advance fee payment (deposit) of £4,000 to secure a place.
totalCostEstimate: £22,000 tuition + London living (UKVI maintenance requirement £1,483/month × 9 = £13,347; realistic London cost £15,000–18,000) ≈ £37,000–£40,000 for the year
scholarshipName: Global Ethnic Majority Music Scholar's Fee Waiver; Sarah Caple Award; Chevening (external)
scholarships: Global Ethnic Majority Music Scholar's Fee Waiver — FULL TUITION waiver; a Tunisian (North African) applicant would plausibly qualify as Global Ethnic Majority, making this the single most realistic Goldsmiths funding route — eligibility criteria and deadline UNVERIFIED, must be checked directly. Sarah Caple Award — amount UNVERIFIED. Chevening (UK government, Tunisia eligible): fully funded, deadline 6 October 2026 for 2027/28 entry, requires 2 years' (2,800 hours) work experience.
englishTest: IELTS 6.5 with 6.5 in writing and no element lower than 6.0
deadline: No fixed deadline; 'Applications accepted from October' and 'We encourage you to complete your application as early as possible.' For 2027 entry applications open around October 2026.

accreditationStatus: Degree awarded by Goldsmiths, University of London
durationEcts: 1 year full-time / 2 years part-time; 180 UK credits (= 90 ECTS)
whatYouStudy: Two pathways: Arts & Practice-Based Research, or Design & Creative Technology. Core modules in programming fundamentals and computational art theory, plus 60 credits of options, culminating in a final exhibition/project (60 credits). Sound and music are among the supported media.
entryRequirements: 'We welcome applications from candidates with a wide range of educational and professional backgrounds.' Prior programming experience is not required: 'The majority of people on the course don't know how to program when they join us.'
acceptsNonMusic: YES — explicitly and unusually open. No music degree, no music portfolio and no prior programming needed. For a software-engineering graduate with no music portfolio yet, this is one of the lowest-barrier Field-A-adjacent routes in London.
portfolioSpec: 'A portfolio of work (supplied as a pdf or a URL linking directly to a relevant web page). The portfolio can be in whatever form you feel is most appropriate (dance, painting, photography, digital art, music, film etc.)' No number of works or duration specified.
auditionSpec: 'Admission to many programmes is by interview, unless you live outside the UK.' No audition.
otherFees: £4,000 advance fee payment (deposit) for international students
totalCostEstimate: ≈ £37,000–£40,000 for the year including London living costs
scholarships: Goldsmiths directs applicants to its scholarship finder — no named award confirmed for this programme, UNVERIFIED. Chevening (Tunisia eligible, fully funded, deadline 6 Oct 2026 for 2027/28, requires 2 years' work experience).
englishTest: IELTS 6.5, with 6.5 in writing and no element lower than 6.0
deadline: 'We will consider applications received before the end of March.'

program: MMus in Composition / Master of Composition (Guildhall Artist) — Electronic & Produced Music department (Electronic Music, Sonic Arts, Live Electronics, Popular Music Production, Produced Music, Game Audio, Film Music)
qualification: Master of Music (MMus) in Composition, or Master of Composition (MComp) [Guildhall Artist]
accreditationStatus: Degrees validated/awarded by Guildhall School of Music & Drama (has UK taught degree-awarding powers)
institutionType: Public (Higher Education Institution funded by the City of London Corporation)
durationEcts: MMus 1 year; MComp 2 years (shared first year with MMus, second year self-directed)
whatYouStudy: Weekly one-to-one Principal Study lessons in Electronic Music — 'Guildhall is unique in offering one-to-one tuition in Electronic Music' — plus five creative projects and electives. MMus students produce 'three portfolios of musical activity: original artistic output, collaborative projects and project leadership'. Intake restricted to 20 students across the four years of the department.
entryRequirements: 'Applicants should normally have obtained an undergraduate degree with Honours in Music, or international equivalent, as a result of completing a minimum of three years in a music college or university music department.' Guildhall's general academic criterion is an Honours undergraduate degree or international equivalent.
acceptsNonMusic: NO as the stated norm — the academic entry criterion explicitly requires a three-year music-college/university-music-department degree. Guildhall does admit on exceptional artistic merit at audition, but this is not published as an entitlement. UNVERIFIED whether a formal exception route exists for a non-music bachelor.
portfolioSpec: EXACTLY, for postgraduate Electronic & Produced Music applicants: (1) a résumé, CV, EPK or similar document detailing your experience; (2) 'Between 5 and 10 minutes of media examples' of your work; (3) a portfolio commentary explaining context and creative processes. 'Quality, creativity and diversity are more important than length.'
auditionSpec: Two stages after portfolio review. (1) CREATIVE EXERCISE: issued about two weeks before interview — produce 'a piece of music of approximately two minutes in length' on your own equipment within a three-hour window; one week to submit via Dropbox. (2) INTERVIEW: held remotely/online in spring 2027 — discussion of your musical and production background, questions on your creative exercise, and your future professional aspirations. Results issued up to 6 weeks after interview.
tuitionNonEU: £32,410 per year (Overseas, MMus 'All Other Pathways' and MComp, students starting September 2026 onwards). The 2027/28 rate is not yet published — UNVERIFIED, but will be at least this.
otherFees: 'All new Postgraduate International entrants are required to pay a 15% non-refundable deposit of tuition fees' (≈ £4,860). Course-related costs £130–£1,500/yr.
totalCostEstimate: £32,410 tuition + London living £1,300–£1,550/month (Guildhall's own figure) ≈ £48,000–£51,000 for one year. MComp doubles this.
scholarships: Departmental partial scholarships: 'When you have been offered and accepted a place at Guildhall you can apply for a partial scholarship within your department' — amounts and deadlines NOT published; UNVERIFIED. Contact music_applications@gsmd.ac.uk. Chevening is the only realistic full-funding route for a Tunisian and would need to be won separately (deadline 6 Oct 2026).
englishTest: UNVERIFIED — no exact IELTS score published on the pages retrieved.
deadline: CURRENT CYCLE FOR SEPTEMBER 2027 ENTRY: application deadline Tuesday 5 January 2027; portfolio submission deadline 12 January 2027; interviews remote/online in spring 2027.

institution: University of Birmingham (Department of Music, home of BEAST — Birmingham ElectroAcoustic Sound Theatre)
program: MA Music: Composition pathway (with Electroacoustic Composition / Sonic Art specialism)
accreditationStatus: Degree awarded by the University of Birmingham
durationEcts: 1 year full-time / 2 years part-time; 180 UK credits (= 90 ECTS) — 120 credits taught plus a 60-credit Composition Portfolio
whatYouStudy: Compulsory: Composition Tutorials 1 & 2 (20 credits each), Composition Portfolio (60), Music Employability (20), Music as Critical Practice (20). Students select 20 credits from electroacoustic or instrumental/vocal composition options, including 'Advanced Studies in Electroacoustic Composition 1 & 2'. Facilities: BEAST 100-channel sound diffusion system, five electroacoustic studios, isolation recording room, dedicated control room, 18-seat computer cluster, Yamaha DM7 console; postgraduate laptop ensemble BEER (Birmingham Ensemble for Electroacoustic Research) covering controller integration, network music and live coding.
entryRequirements: 'A 2:1 Honours Degree (or international equivalent) in a relevant subject.' Plus portfolio.
acceptsNonMusic: PARTIALLY — 'We can consider an Honours degree in another subject if you have significant professional musical experience and relevant qualifications.' Quoted verbatim. For a candidate with NO professional musical experience and NO portfolio, this route is currently closed; it would open only after building a body of work.
portfolioSpec: 'All applicants for the composition pathway must submit a portfolio of 3–4 compositions, showcasing your range of styles and compositional technique, submitted as either scores (PDF files) or recordings.' Audio/video uploaded to SoundCloud/MixCloud, YouTube/Vimeo/Youku or Dropbox/WeTransfer, with the URL pasted into a text document uploaded to the application portal.
auditionSpec: No audition specified — selection on portfolio and application.
tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED — the course page shows UK/Ireland fees of £11,250 full-time but does not state the international rate on the retrieved page. Birmingham's 2026/27 international MA Music rate is in the ~£23,000–£26,000 range at comparable Russell Group departments; DO NOT rely on this without checking. International students must also pay a tuition fee deposit before a CAS is issued.
otherFees: Tuition fee deposit required before CAS issue — amount UNVERIFIED
scholarshipName: Birmingham Masters Scholarship; Music Masters Scholarships; Chevening (external)
scholarships: Birmingham Masters Scholarship — £3,000 fee discount. Music Masters Scholarships — varying awards, amounts UNVERIFIED. Neither approaches full funding for an overseas fee. Chevening remains the only realistic full-funding route for a Tunisian.
englishTest: IELTS 6.5 with no less than 6.0 in any band
deadline: 28 August 2026 (for 2026/27 entry). PRIOR CYCLE — expect a comparable late-August 2027 deadline, but apply far earlier for visa and funding reasons.
applicationOpens: Typically autumn of the preceding year — UNVERIFIED

institution: University of Edinburgh — Edinburgh College of Art / Reid School of Music
accreditationStatus: Degree awarded by the University of Edinburgh
durationEcts: 1 year full-time / 2 years part-time; 180 UK credits (= 90 ECTS)
whatYouStudy: Film sound, interactive game-audio design, sound installation and sonic art, sound software design, and creative music practices. Skills in digital audio workstations, microphone techniques, mixing, spatialisation, and creative coding for sound.
entryRequirements: 'A UK 2:1 honours degree, or its international equivalent, in a relevant subject such as music, sound design, media arts, sound engineering, acoustics, film, animation, and art and design.' AND, verbatim: 'We also welcome applicants who do not meet academic entry requirements but demonstrate relevant professional experience.'
acceptsNonMusic: PARTIALLY-TO-YES — the listed relevant subjects are broad (media arts, film, animation, art and design) and Edinburgh explicitly welcomes applicants who do not meet the academic requirement but show relevant professional experience. A software-engineering BSc is not on the list, so admission would rest on the portfolio.
portfolioSpec: 'You must submit a portfolio as part of your application.' It should include 'at least three pieces of work' — sound design examples for films, games, animations, essays on sound, or documentation of sound-based projects. Work must be your own; for collaborative projects a brief explanation of your role is required. Submit as a single PDF (max 4MB, or a link if larger); audio/video hosted online with links provided.
tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED — the international rate is not stated on the retrieved programme page. For comparison, Edinburgh's MSc Acoustics and Music Technology international rate is quoted at £25,100 (aggregator source, UNVERIFIED).
totalCostEstimate: Tuition UNVERIFIED + Edinburgh living costs, which the University itself estimates at '£18,504 each year' for a postgraduate (2026-2027).
scholarshipName: Edinburgh College of Art scholarships; Chevening (external)
scholarships: 'Edinburgh College of Art scholarships' are signposted on the programme page — names, amounts and deadlines UNVERIFIED. Chevening (Tunisia eligible).

deadline: PRIOR CYCLE (Sept 2026 entry) rounds: Round 1 apply by 15 December 2025, decisions by 19 March 2026; Round 2 apply by 4 May 2026, decisions by 30 June 2026. Expect equivalent rounds opening around October 2026 for September 2027.

institution: University of York — School of Arts and Creative Technologies

accreditationStatus: Degree awarded by the University of York
durationEcts: 1 year full-time / 2 years part-time; 180 UK credits (= 90 ECTS)
whatYouStudy: Core modules: Audio Cultures and Modernities; Audio Signals and Psychoacoustics; Production Techniques for Acoustic Recording; Research Approaches and Processes; Spatial Audio & Surround Sound; Studio Live and Analogue Mixing. Substantial Research Project in a chosen specialism.
entryRequirements: Normally a degree in music or a related subject. Verbatim: 'We will also consider unrelated first degrees provided you can demonstrate a good grasp of music theory and some practical ability in music making.'
acceptsNonMusic: YES — with a condition. Quoted: 'We will also consider unrelated first degrees provided you can demonstrate a good grasp of music theory and some practical ability in music making.' The music-theory requirement is a genuine hurdle for a candidate with no conservatoire training, but it is an explicit, published route.
portfolioSpec: EXACTLY: 'a short portfolio of 2 music tracks (no longer than 10 minutes in total) that you recorded/produced, edited, and mixed, with a written commentary (maximum 500 words).' Tracks in .wav format; mp3 at 320 kb/s acceptable if upload limits require it.

accreditationStatus: Degree awarded by the University of Westminster
durationEcts: 1 year full-time (part-time day option); 180 UK credits (= 90 ECTS)
whatYouStudy: Core: Creative Music Production; Major Project (60 credits); Interactive Audio for Games; Audio-visual Production and Sound Design; Research Methods: Theory and Practice; Entrepreneurship and Innovation. entryRequirements: Verbatim: 'A minimum of a lower second class honours degree (2:2) or lower with substantial experience.' Plus a portfolio and a personal statement.

portfolioSpec: 'A portfolio of audio and/or audio visual production works, demonstrating your potential to work in audio at a high level.' Number of works, duration and format NOT specified — UNVERIFIED.

tuitionNonEU: £16,000 per academic year (International). 'Fees remain fixed throughout your studies.' — the LOWEST international fee found for a credible London audio-production MA.
totalCostEstimate: £16,000 tuition + London living (UKVI maintenance £1,483/month × 9 = £13,347) ≈ £29,000–£34,000 for the year

scholarships: 'The university offers a variety of scholarships to eligible postgraduate students' — specific schemes, amounts and deadlines UNVERIFIED and must be checked. deadline: UNVERIFIED — 'information available on the How to apply page'.
